channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Resonating-valence-bond superconductor from small Fermi surface in twisted bilayer graphene
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76586-1

Whether superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene emerges from small or large Fermi surfaces remains debated. Here, the authors propose a symmetric pseudogap metal with small hole pockets, showing that local-moment pairing can transfer to mobile carriers and yield two-gap nematic superconductivity
item.dc:title: Resonating-valence-bond superconductor from small Fermi surface in twisted bilayer graphene
item.dc:creator: Jing-Yu Zhao
Ya-Hui Zhang

item.title: Uncoupling of the allosteric signalling network in the β<sub>1</sub>-adrenergic receptor by a negative allosteric modulator
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77802-8

Understanding allosteric modulation mechanisms at G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) is key to development of therapeutics. Here, the authors show how a negative allosteric modulator acts to uncouple the signalling network of β1-adrenergic receptor.
item.dc:title: Uncoupling of the allosteric signalling network in the β<sub>1</sub>-adrenergic receptor by a negative allosteric modulator

item.title: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77838-w

BEAR-GRN provides a standardized framework for benchmarking gene regulatory network inference methods using single-cell multi-omics data, revealing that ground-truth choice profoundly impacts performance and that current methods remain predominantly RNA-driven.
item.dc:title: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods

item.title: Genome-wide cross-trait analysis to compare genetic architecture between Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77920-3

Parkinson’s disease has been epidemiologically linked to kidney function, but the extent of their shared genetic basis remains unclear. Here, the authors integrate genome-wide genetic correlation, pleiotropy and colocalisation analyses to identify shared loci and candidate pathways connecting Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits.
item.dc:title: Genome-wide cross-trait analysis to compare genetic architecture between Parkinson’s disease and kidney-related traits

item.title: Learning chemical-induced gene expression perturbations with WAVE
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77645-3

Drug-induced gene expression profiles can reveal compound mechanisms but are difficult to generate at scale. Here, the authors present WAVE, a deep learning model that accurately predicts bulk and single-cell drug responses, with experimental validation supporting its potential for drug discovery.
item.dc:title: Learning chemical-induced gene expression perturbations with WAVE

item.title: Cell-type-specific surfaceome profiling of 100-500 isolated cells using a droplet-based Magnetic Affinity Purification System
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77876-4

Surface proteins are a key source of biomarkers and therapeutic targets, but remain poorly characterized in disease-relevant cells. Here, authors developed nanoMAPS, an ultrasensitive proteomic method to profile surface proteins from hundreds of primary cells and identify potential biomarkers.
item.dc:title: Cell-type-specific surfaceome profiling of 100-500 isolated cells using a droplet-based Magnetic Affinity Purification System

item.title: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77930-1

Deep-learning segmentation accuracy depends on image resolution, with each architecture having an optimum, usually at a lower microscopy resolution. Here, the authors present ReScale4DL, a framework for optimising imaging experiments by selecting resolutions to balance accuracy, throughput and cost.
item.dc:title: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation

item.title: Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77553-6

Here, the authors develop injectable arterial organoids that form functional vascular networks in vivo, promoting blood flow restoration and tissue repair in models of ischemic disease by enhancing vascular regeneration.
item.dc:title: Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases
